Base directory for this skill: /Users/owner/.claude/skills/video-use # video-use (bootstrap + operating mode + HyperFrames graphics + field notes) This skill installs the open-source editor https://github.com/browser-use/video-use and uses its own SKILL.md for the editing method, with two changes: it runs start to finish on judgment without asking questions (§0), and it builds graphics with HyperFrames (§3). Where this file and the upstream SKILL.md disagree, this file wins. ## 0. Operating mode: judgment, not questions Upstream is built around ask → confirm → execute. Here it runs straight through. - **No questions.** Don't call AskUserQuestion and don't end a turn on a question. Wherever upstream says ask, propose and wait, confirm, or let the user choose (process steps 3–4, Hard Rule 11, the palette, the music bed, the delivery format, "continue the last session?", "final render on confirmation"), decide with the defaults below and record the decision. - **Hard Rule 11 becomes "plan before cutting".** Write the strategy (4–8 sentences, as in upstream step 4) to `/project.md` before touching the cut, opening with an `Assumptions:` line for anything you had to guess. Then execute. Hard Rules 1–10 and 12 still hold. - **Read before deciding:** the user's message; `/project.md` (carry earlier sessions' canvas, fonts, palette and caption look forward unless told otherwise); any brief, notes, brand files or reference videos in the footage folder; and the footage itself (packed transcript plus `timeline_view` at decision points). - **Ambiguity → the most likely reading**, stated once in the hand-off. Vague feedback ("make it pop") → pick the most likely element, change one thing, say which. - **Stop only for a real blocker, and report it rather than ask:** no footage reachable, no transcription path when the edit depends on speech (§2), every source unreadable. First finish everything that doesn't depend on it (probe, inventory, contact sheet), then say in one or two lines what is missing and what it unblocks. - **Nothing irreversible:** sources are read-only, outputs go to `edit/`, and an earlier final is never overwritten (write `final_v2.mp4`). - **Deliver finished work.** After self-eval passes, plus the critic pass for anything that will be posted (reels, promos, ads), render the final, not just a preview. The hand-off is the file, its actual duration, aspect and loudness, the assumptions made, and anything left undone. ### Defaults when nothing says otherwise | Decision | Default | |---|---| | Canvas | Vertical source, or "reel / short / TikTok / story" → 1080×1920. Otherwise match the source aspect. Square or 4:5 only when asked. Changing aspect needs Mode B (§3.1). | | Length | Reels 20–45 s: keep the best, not everything. Long-form: tighten pauses and retakes, keep every point. Montage: the music's length, or ~30 s. | | fps | Match the source. | | Language | Detected from speech; captions in the spoken language. Hebrew → `--language he`. | | Captions | On for anything with speech headed to social; off for a wordless montage. 2–3 words a line, active-word highlight. Hebrew, Arabic or mixed lines → HyperFrames captions (§3.4). | | Hook | Open on the strongest line, with no title card in front of it. | | Grade | `none`, unless frames show a real problem (underexposure, colour cast, flat log) → a corrective grade only, checked on skin. | | Music | Only files the user supplied (footage folder or chat). Never download or generate music unasked; with no music file, ship without and say so. Several files → pick the one that fits the pacing and note the other. Duck under speech. | | SFX | Only when tied to a visible event; skip without a library. | | Graphics | §3.1, restraint first. | | Look | Brand files or `project.md` first. Otherwise one accent (sampled from the footage, or `#FFD60A`), white text with a soft shadow, Heebo 800 for Hebrew/mixed or Inter for English-only. Record it in `project.md` as the house style. | | Deliverables | `final.mp4` (H.264, yuv420p, AAC, −14 LUFS / −1 dBTP) plus `final.srt` when captions are burned in. | ## 1. Install (once per session) ```bash test -d ~/Developer/video-use || git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/browser-use/video-use ~/Developer/video-use cd ~/Developer/video-use && (uv sync || pip install -e .) mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills && ln -sfn ~/Developer/video-use ~/.claude/skills/video-use ~/Developer/video-use/.venv/bin/python ~/Developer/video-use/helpers/timeline_view.py --help >/dev/null && ffprobe -version | head -1 ``` Then **read `~/Developer/video-use/SKILL.md` in full** and follow it as amended by §0 and §3. Helpers live in `~/Developer/video-use/helpers/`. Run them with the repo's `.venv/bin/python`. Set up HyperFrames (§3.2) as soon as the plan includes a graphic. ## 2. ElevenLabs key + network - Transcription needs `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY`, from the environment or `~/Developer/video-use/.env`. If neither has it and the edit depends on speech, that is a §0 blocker: do the inventory, then say the key is needed (pasted in chat, or put in that `.env`). When the user pastes one, write it with `chmod 600`. Never echo the key, and never write it into the footage folder. An edit without speech (a music montage) goes ahead untranscribed. - The cloud workspace blocks `api.elevenlabs.io` unless the user adds it under claude.ai Settings → Capabilities → allowed domains. Test with `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/models`. `000` means blocked: report it as a blocker and name the domain to allow. `401 missing_permissions` on /v1/user or /v1/models is fine for a scoped key: speech-to-text still works. - Hugging Face and the OpenAI model CDNs are blocked too, so there is no offline Whisper fallback (HyperFrames' own `transcribe` downloads its models from Hugging Face as well). Don't hunt for model mirrors. - Hebrew: pass `--language he`. Scribe diarization separates an off-camera producer (S0) from the speaker (S1), which is useful for dropping interruptions. ## 3. Graphics with HyperFrames HyperFrames (`heygen-com/hyperframes`) renders an HTML page with a paused GSAP timeline to video, frame by frame in headless Chrome. Upstream already lists it as one animation engine; here it is the default for graphics. Everything in §3 was checked end to end with CLI 0.8.180 (Oct 2026) in the cloud workspace: slot render, alpha composite through render.py's exact filter, Hebrew and mixed-language text, the caption layer. The CLI ships almost daily, so when a flag here disagrees with `npx hyperframes --help`, trust `--help`. ### 3.1 Judgment: what, which engine, which mode **What earns a graphic:** a hook title when the opening line doesn't hook on its own; a lower third the first time a person or product is named; a callout when the speaker says a number, a list or a step; an end card when there is a call to action. At most one new graphic element every ~3 s, the payoff landing on the spoken word (upstream's payoff-timing rule), the final frame held ≥ 1 s. No graphics at all when the footage carries itself. | Engine | Use for | |---|---| | **HyperFrames** (default) | Anything with text or layout: titles, lower thirds, callouts, counters and stats, lists, charts, end cards, follow/subscribe cards, progress bars, kinetic type, any Hebrew/RTL text, styled captions. Check the registry first (§3.3). | | Manim | Equations, formal diagrams, graph morphs (upstream vendors a Manim skill). | | PIL | A trivial static card, or when no Chrome can run at all. | | Remotion | Only if asked, or an existing Remotion brand system is in play. | **Mode A, overlay slots (default).** video-use owns the picture (cut, grade, HDR tone-map, scale, mix). Each graphic is a transparent HyperFrames clip that `render.py` composites. Right whenever graphics sit on top of the footage. **Mode B, HyperFrames finish.** video-use makes the cut decisions and HyperFrames composes the final. Choose it when graphics have to move or reframe the footage itself: changing aspect (render.py only scales, it never crops, so 16:9 footage stays 16:9), punch-ins, split-screen or picture-in-picture, B-roll moving with graphics, shader transitions. Also choose it when there are more than ~8 graphic elements. See §3.5. ### 3.2 Environment ```bash export HYPERFRAMES_NO_TELEMETRY=1 HYPERFRAMES_SKIP_SKILLS=1 # init's --skip-skills flag is ignored; the env var works npx --yes hyperframes browser ensure || \ export HYPERFRAMES_BROWSER_PATH=$(ls -d /opt/pw-browsers/chromium_headless_shell-*/chrome-linux/headless_shell | tail -1) ``` - In the cloud workspace `browser ensure` fails (storage.googleapis.com is blocked), but a Playwright headless shell is preinstalled under `/opt/pw-browsers/`, which is the fallback above. Node 22 and ffmpeg are present. Re-export these variables in every Bash call and every sub-agent brief, because shell state doesn't persist. - `cdn.jsdelivr.net` is blocked, and the `init` scaffold and every registry block load GSAP from it, so their renders fail. Vendor GSAP and fonts once into `/animations/_shared/` and copy them into every slot: ```bash SH=/animations/_shared; mkdir -p $SH/vendor $SH/assets/fonts && cd $SH [ -f vendor/gsap.min.js ] || { npm pack gsap@3 --silent >/dev/null && tar -xzf gsap-*.tgz && cp package/dist/gsap.min.js vendor/ && rm -rf package gsap-*.tgz; } [ -f assets/fonts/heebo-hebrew-800-normal.woff2 ] || { npm pack @fontsource/heebo --silent >/dev/null && tar -xzf fontsource-heebo-*.tgz && cp package/files/heebo-{hebrew,latin}-{400,800}-normal.woff2 assets/fonts/ && rm -rf package fontsource-heebo-*.tgz; } ``` Then write `assets/fonts/heebo.css` with one `@font-face` per weight and subset, `url("heebo-hebrew-800-normal.woff2")` style paths (relative to the CSS file), `font-display: block`, Hebrew `unicode-range: U+0307-0308, U+0590-05FF, U+200C-2010, U+20AA, U+25CC, U+FB1D-FB4F`, Latin `unicode-range: U+0000-00FF, U+0131, U+0152-0153, U+02BB-02BC, U+02C6, U+02DA, U+02DC, U+2000-206F, U+20AC, U+2122, U+2212, U+FEFF, U+FFFD`. Other Fontsource families work the same way (`rubik`, `assistant`, `noto-sans-hebrew`, `frank-ruhl-libre`). Inter, Roboto, Montserrat, Poppins and Oswald are bundled and need no file. - A slot needs no `init`: a folder holding `index.html`, `vendor/` and `assets/` renders. - Speed here: about 6 s of wall time per second of 1080×1920 alpha output (2 cores, screenshot capture). A full-length caption layer for a 40 s reel takes 4–5 min. Parallel slot renders share the CPU. - On the user's Mac `browser ensure` and jsDelivr work, but vendoring still costs nothing and keeps renders offline and deterministic, so do it there too. ### 3.3 Mode A: one slot, end to end 1. **Canvas = the base render.py builds,** because it overlays at 0,0 without scaling. Portrait sources become 1920 tall and landscape sources 1920 wide, the other side following the source aspect (ffprobe the source, mind rotation tags). Build every slot full-frame at exactly that size, transparent everywhere except the graphic. `render.py --draft` builds a 1280 base, so overlays land wrong there: check overlays with `--preview`. 2. **Scaffold:** `mkdir -p /animations/slot_ && cd /animations/slot_ && cp -r ../_shared/vendor ../_shared/assets .`, then write `index.html` from the skeleton below. 3. **Registry first.** `npx hyperframes catalog --query "" --json` (447 items; works here), then `npx hyperframes add --no-clipboard`, which installs `compositions/.html` and prints a mount snippet. After adding: point GSAP at the vendored copy (`sed -i 's#https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/gsap@[^"]*/dist/gsap.min.js#vendor/gsap.min.js#' compositions/*.html`); replace placeholder text, avatars and colours; give the mount `data-start`, `data-duration` (≥ the block's own length) and a z-index, which the snippet lacks; rename the block's composition id in its file and mount if it is `main`; most blocks are 1920×1080, so prefer portrait ones for 9:16 or scale them in a wrapper. Useful for reels: `lt-clean-bar`, `lt-soft-pill`, `lt-dark-card`, `headline-slam`, `per-word-rise`, `titlecard-lockup`, `count-up`, `mk-progress-stat`, `chart-story`, `cta-lockup`, `cta-close`, `instagram-follow`, `tiktok-follow`. 4. **Check and render:** ```bash npx hyperframes lint # 0 errors npx hyperframes snapshot --at , -o snaps # transparency shows as white here: judge white text in the composite instead npx hyperframes render --format mov -o render.mov # ProRes 4444 with alpha ffprobe -v error -show_entries stream=pix_fmt,width,height -show_entries format=duration -of compact render.mov ``` Gate: `pix_fmt` starts with `yuva` (it is `yuva444p12le`), the size equals the base, the duration equals the slot length. 5. **EDL entry:** `{"file": "/abs/path/to/edit/animations/slot_/render.mov", "start_in_output": T, "duration": D}`. Use absolute paths: render.py resolves overlay paths against the EDL's own folder, so upstream's `edit/animations/…` example becomes `edit/edit/…`. List order is stacking order (later is on top). `T` = the payoff word's output time minus the reveal time. 6. **Never `.webm` for render.py overlays.** Verified: ffmpeg's default VP9 decoder drops the alpha, and during the overlay window the whole frame turns black. MOV only. Skeleton (1080×1920; change the four size spots for another base): ```html
3 טעויות שכולם עושים
``` Rules that break slot renders (condensed from the edit-video skill's §0): - The root needs `data-composition-id`, `data-width`, `data-height` and `data-duration`. The render length is the root `data-duration`, never the GSAP length. - One paused timeline, registered after the last tween as `window.__timelines[""]`. A key that doesn't match the id makes the render wait ~45 s and then freeze. - Deterministic only: no `Math.random`, `Date`, `performance.now`, `requestAnimationFrame`, CSS `transition` or `repeat: -1`. 1	---
2	name: video-use
3	description: Edit any video by conversation. Transcribe, cut, color grade, generate overlay animations, burn subtitles — for talking heads, montages, tutorials, travel, interviews. No presets, no menus. Ask questions, confirm the plan, execute, iterate, persist. Production-correctness rules are hard; everything else is artistic freedom.
4	---
5	
6	# Video Use
7	
8	## Principle
9	
10	1. **LLM reasons from raw transcript + on-demand visuals.** The only derived artifact that earns its keep is a packed phrase-level transcript (`takes_packed.md`). Everything else — filler tagging, retake detection, shot classification, emphasis scoring — you derive at decision time.
11	2. **Audio is primary, visuals follow.** Cut candidates come from speech boundaries and silence gaps. Drill into visuals only at decision points.
12	3. **Ask → confirm → execute → iterate → persist.** Never touch the cut until the user has confirmed the strategy in plain English.
13	4. **Generalize.** Do not assume what kind of video this is. Look at the material, ask the user, then edit.
14	5. **Artistic freedom is the default.** Every specific value, preset, font, color, duration, pitch structure, and technique in this document is a *worked example* from one proven video — not a mandate. Read them to understand what's possible and why each worked. Then make your own taste calls based on what the material actually is and what the user actually wants. **The only things you MUST do are in the Hard Rules section below.** Everything else is yours.
15	6. **Invent freely.** If the material calls for a technique not described here — split-screen, picture-in-picture, lower-third identity cards, reaction cuts, speed ramps, freeze frames, crossfades, match cuts, L-cuts, J-cuts, speed ramps over breath, whatever — build it. The helpers are ffmpeg and PIL. They can do anything the format supports. Do not wait for permission.
16	7. **Verify your own output before showing it to the user.** If you wouldn't ship it, don't present it.
17	
18	## Hard Rules (production correctness — non-negotiable)
19	
20	These are the things where deviation produces silent failures or broken output. They are not taste, they are correctness. Memorize them.
21	
22	1. **Subtitles are applied LAST in the filter chain**, after every overlay. Otherwise overlays hide captions. Silent failure.
23	2. **Per-segment extract → lossless `-c copy` concat**, not single-pass filtergraph. Otherwise you double-encode every segment when overlays are added.
24	3. **30ms audio fades at every segment boundary** (`afade=t=in:st=0:d=0.03,afade=t=out:st={dur-0.03}:d=0.03`). Otherwise audible pops at every cut.
25	4. **Overlays use `setpts=PTS-STARTPTS+T/TB`** to shift the overlay's frame 0 to its window start. Otherwise you see the middle of the animation during the overlay window.
26	5. **Master SRT uses output-timeline offsets**: `output_time = word.start - segment_start + segment_offset`. Otherwise captions misalign after segment concat.
27	6. **Never cut inside a word.** Snap every cut edge to a word boundary from the Scribe transcript.
28	7. **Pad every cut edge.** Working window: 30–200ms. Scribe timestamps drift 50–100ms — padding absorbs the drift. Tighter for fast-paced, looser for cinematic.
29	8. **Word-level verbatim ASR only.** Never SRT/phrase mode (loses sub-second gap data). Never normalized fillers (loses editorial signal).
30	9. **Cache transcripts per source.** Never re-transcribe unless the source file itself changed.
31	10. **Parallel sub-agents for multiple animations.** Never sequential. Spawn N at once via the `Agent` tool; total wall time ≈ slowest one.
32	11. **Strategy confirmation before execution.** Never touch the cut until the user has approved the plain-English plan.
33	12. **All session outputs in `<videos_dir>/edit/`.** Never write inside the `video-use/` project directory.
34	
35	Everything else in this document is a worked example. Deviate whenever the material calls for it.
36	
37	## Directory layout
38	
39	The skill lives in `video-use/`. User footage lives wherever they put it. All session outputs go into `<videos_dir>/edit/`.
40	
41	```
42	<videos_dir>/
43	├── <source files, untouched>
44	└── edit/
45	    ├── project.md               ← memory; appended every session
46	    ├── takes_packed.md          ← phrase-level transcripts, the LLM's primary reading view
47	    ├── edl.json                 ← cut decisions
48	    ├── transcripts/<name>.json  ← cached raw Scribe JSON
49	    ├── animations/slot_<id>/    ← per-animation source + render + reasoning
50	    ├── clips_graded/            ← per-segment extracts with grade + fades
51	    ├── master.srt               ← output-timeline subtitles
52	    ├── downloads/               ← yt-dlp outputs
53	    ├── verify/                  ← debug frames / timeline PNGs
54	    ├── preview.mp4
55	    └── final.mp4
56	```
57	
58	## Setup
59	
60	First-time install lives in `install.md` (clone, deps, ffmpeg, skill registration, API key). Don't re-run it every session; on cold start just verify:
61	
62	- `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY` resolves — either in the environment or in `.env` at the video-use repo root. If missing, ask the user to paste one and write it to `.env` (never to the user's `<videos_dir>`).
63	- `ffmpeg` + `ffprobe` on PATH.
64	- Python deps installed (`uv sync` or `pip install -e .` inside the repo).
65	- Node.js + npm available if the session needs HyperFrames or Remotion slots. HyperFrames currently requires Node.js 22+.
66	- `yt-dlp`, HyperFrames, Remotion, Manim installed only on first use.
67	- First-use animation setup happens inside the slot directory, never at the video-use repo root. HyperFrames can be invoked with `npx --yes hyperframes ...`; Remotion can be scaffolded with `npx create-video@latest` or installed as a project-local dependency before using its `remotion render` command.
68	- This skill vendors `skills/manim-video/`. Read its SKILL.md when building a Manim slot.
69	
70	Helpers (`helpers/transcribe.py`, `helpers/render.py`, etc.) live alongside this SKILL.md. Resolve their paths relative to the directory containing this file — the skill is typically symlinked at `~/.claude/skills/video-use/` or `~/.codex/skills/video-use/`.
71	
72	## Helpers
73	
74	- **`transcribe.py <video>`** — single-file Scribe call. `--num-speakers N` optional. Cached.
75	- **`transcribe_batch.py <videos_dir>`** — 4-worker parallel transcription. Use for multi-take.
76	- **`pack_transcripts.py --edit-dir <dir>`** — `transcripts/*.json` → `takes_packed.md` (phrase-level, break on silence ≥ 0.5s).
77	- **`timeline_view.py <video> <start> <end>`** — filmstrip + waveform PNG. On-demand visual drill-down. **Not a scan tool** — use it at decision points, not constantly.
78	- **`render.py <edl.json> -o <out>`** — per-segment extract → concat → overlays (PTS-shifted) → subtitles LAST. `--preview` for 720p fast. `--build-subtitles` to generate master.srt inline.
79	- **`grade.py <in> -o <out>`** — ffmpeg filter chain grade. Presets + `--filter '<raw>'` for custom.
80	
81	For animations, create `<edit>/animations/slot_<id>/` with `Bash` and spawn a sub-agent via the `Agent` tool.
82	
83	## The process
84	
85	1. **Inventory.** `ffprobe` every source. `transcribe_batch.py` on the directory. `pack_transcripts.py` to produce `takes_packed.md`. Sample one or two `timeline_view`s for a visual first impression.
86	2. **Pre-scan for problems.** One pass over `takes_packed.md` to note verbal slips, obvious mis-speaks, or phrasings to avoid. Plain list, feed into the editor brief.
87	3. **Converse.** Describe what you see in plain English. Ask questions *shaped by the material*. Collect: content type, target length/aspect, aesthetic/brand direction, pacing feel, must-preserve moments, must-cut moments, animation and grade preferences, subtitle needs. Do not use a fixed checklist — the right questions are different every time.
88	4. **Propose strategy.** 4–8 sentences: shape, take choices, cut direction, animation plan, grade direction, subtitle style, length estimate. **Wait for confirmation.**
89	5. **Execute.** Produce `edl.json` via the editor sub-agent brief. Drill into `timeline_view` at ambiguous moments. Build animations in parallel sub-agents. Apply grade per-segment. Compose via `render.py`.
90	6. **Preview.** `render.py --preview`.
91	7. **Self-eval (before showing the user).** Run `timeline_view` on the **rendered output** (not the sources) at every cut boundary (±1.5s window). Check each image for:
92	   - Visual discontinuity / flash / jump at the cut
93	   - Waveform spike at the boundary (audio pop that slipped past the 30ms fade)
94	   - Subtitle hidden behind an overlay (Rule 1 violation)
95	   - Overlay misaligned or showing wrong frames (Rule 4 violation)
96	
97	   Also sample: first 2s, last 2s, and 2–3 mid-points — check grade consistency, subtitle readability, overall coherence. Run `ffprobe` on the output to verify duration matches the EDL expectation.
98	
99	   Measure the audio, don't assume it: `ffmpeg -i out.mp4 -af ebur128=peak=true -f null -` for integrated loudness and true peak, plus RMS per section (dialogue, music-only, end card). An end card 15 dB under the dialogue, or effects louder than speech, is a bug. You cannot listen: say so, and report the numbers.
100	
101	   For anything the user will publish (launch, promo, ad), also spawn one **critic sub-agent** with the rendered file, the EDL, and any reference videos the user gave. Brief it to roast, not to praise: a verdict, ranked problems with timecodes and evidence (frames, levels), and the 5 fixes to do first. Fresh eyes catch what the author stopped seeing — cut-off payoff lines, 0.5s memes, unreadable 28px text at phone size.
102	
103	   If anything fails: fix → re-render → re-eval. **Cap at 3 self-eval passes** — if issues remain after 3, flag them to the user rather than looping forever. Only present the preview once the self-eval passes.
104	8. **Iterate + persist.** Natural-language feedback, re-plan, re-render. Never re-transcribe. Final render on confirmation. Append to `project.md`.
105	
106	## Cut craft (techniques)
107	
108	- **Audio-first.** Candidate cuts from word boundaries and silence gaps.
109	- **Preserve peaks.** Laughs, punchlines, emphasis beats. Extend past punchlines to include reactions — the laugh IS the beat.
110	- **Speaker handoffs** benefit from air between utterances. Common values: 400–600ms. Less for fast-paced, more for cinematic. Taste call.
111	- **Audio events as signals.** `(laughs)`, `(sighs)`, `(applause)` mark beats. Extend past them.
112	- **Silence gaps are cut candidates.** Silences ≥400ms are usually the cleanest. 150–400ms phrase boundaries are usable with a visual check. <150ms is unsafe (mid-phrase).
113	- **Example cut padding** (the launch video shipped with this): 50ms before the first kept word, 80ms after the last. Tighter for montage energy, looser for documentary. Stay in the 30–200ms working window (Hard Rule 7).
114	- **Never reason audio and video independently.** Every cut must work on both tracks.
115	
116	## The packed transcript (primary reading view)
117	
118	`pack_transcripts.py` reads all `transcripts/*.json` and produces one markdown file where each take is a list of phrase-level lines, each prefixed with its `[start-end]` time range. Phrases break on any silence ≥ 0.5s OR speaker change. This is the artifact the editor sub-agent reads to pick cuts — it gives word-boundary precision from text alone at 1/10 the tokens of raw JSON.
119	
120	Example line:
121	```
122	## C0103  (duration: 43.0s, 8 phrases)
123	  [002.52-005.36] S0 Ninety percent of what a web agent does is completely wasted.
124	  [006.08-006.74] S0 We fixed this.
125	```
126	
127	## Editor sub-agent brief (for multi-take selection)
128	
129	When the task is "pick the best take of each beat across many clips," spawn a dedicated sub-agent with a brief shaped like this. The structure is load-bearing; the pitch-shape example is not.
130	
131	```
132	You are editing a <type> video. Pick the best take of each beat and 
133	assemble them chronologically by beat, not by source clip order.
134	
135	INPUTS:
136	  - takes_packed.md (time-annotated phrase-level transcripts of all takes)
137	  - Product/narrative context: <2 sentences from the user>
138	  - Speaker(s): <name, role, delivery style note>
139	  - Expected structure: <pick an archetype or invent one>
140	  - Verbal slips to avoid: <list from the pre-scan pass>
141	  - Target runtime: <seconds>
142	
143	Common structural archetypes (pick, adapt, or invent):
144	  - Tech launch / demo:   HOOK → PROBLEM → SOLUTION → BENEFIT → EXAMPLE → CTA
145	  - Tutorial:             INTRO → SETUP → STEPS → GOTCHAS → RECAP
146	  - Interview:            (QUESTION → ANSWER → FOLLOWUP) repeat
147	  - Travel / event:       ARRIVAL → HIGHLIGHTS → QUIET MOMENTS → DEPARTURE
148	  - Documentary:          THESIS → EVIDENCE → COUNTERPOINT → CONCLUSION
149	  - Music / performance:  INTRO → VERSE → CHORUS → BRIDGE → OUTRO
150	  - Or invent your own.
151	
152	RULES:
153	  - Start/end times must fall on word boundaries from the transcript.
154	  - Pad cut boundaries (working window 30–200ms).
155	  - Prefer silences ≥ 400ms as cut targets.
156	  - Unavoidable slips are kept if no better take exists. Note them in "reason".
157	  - If over budget, revise: drop a beat or trim tails. Report total and self-correct.
158	
159	OUTPUT (JSON array, no prose):
160	  [{"source": "C0103", "start": 2.42, "end": 6.85, "beat": "HOOK",
161	    "quote": "...", "reason": "..."}, ...]
162	
163	Return the final EDL and a one-line total runtime check.
164	```
165	
166	## Color grade (when requested)
167	
168	Your job is to **reason about the image**, not apply a preset. Look at a frame (via `timeline_view`), decide what's wrong, adjust one thing, look again.
169	
170	Mental model is ASC CDL. Per channel: `out = (in * slope + offset) ** power`, then global saturation. `slope` → highlights, `offset` → shadows, `power` → midtones.
171	
172	**Example filter chains** (`grade.py` has `--list-presets`; use them as starting points or mix your own):
173	
174	- **`warm_cinematic`** — retro/technical, subtle teal/orange split, desaturated. Shipped in a real launch video. Safe for talking heads.
175	- **`neutral_punch`** — minimal corrective: contrast bump + gentle S-curve. No hue shifts.
176	- **`none`** — straight copy. Default when the user hasn't asked.
177	
178	For anything else — portraiture, nature, product, music video, documentary — invent your own chain. `grade.py --filter '<raw ffmpeg>'` accepts any filter string.
179	
180	Hard rules: apply **per-segment during extraction** (not post-concat, which re-encodes twice). Never go aggressive without testing skin tones.
181	
182	## Subtitles (when requested)
183	
184	Subtitles have three dimensions worth reasoning about: **chunking** (1/2/3/sentence per line), **case** (UPPER/Title/Natural), and **placement** (margin from bottom). The right combo depends on content.
185	
186	**Worked styles** — pick, adapt, or invent:
187	
188	**`bold-overlay`** — short-form tech launch, fast-paced social. ~2-word chunks, UPPERCASE, break on punctuation and pauses ≥ 0.3s, grow to 3 words rather than flash a cue < 0.35s (`chunk_words` in `render.py`), Helvetica 18 Bold, white-on-outline, `MarginV=35`. `render.py` ships with this as `SUB_FORCE_STYLE`.
189	
190	```
191	FontName=Helvetica,FontSize=18,Bold=1,
192	PrimaryColour=&H00FFFFFF,OutlineColour=&H00000000,BackColour=&H00000000,
193	BorderStyle=1,Outline=2,Shadow=0,
194	Alignment=2,MarginV=35
195	```
196	
197	**`natural-sentence`** (if you invent this mode) — narrative, documentary, education. 4–7 word chunks, sentence case, break on natural pauses, `MarginV=60–80`, larger font for readability, slightly wider max-width. No shipped force_style — design one if you need it.
198	
199	Invent a third style if neither fits. Hard rules: subtitles LAST (Rule 1), output-timeline offsets (Rule 5).
200	
201	## Animations (when requested)
202	
203	Animations match the content and the brand. **Get the palette, font, and visual language from the conversation** — never assume a default. If the user hasn't told you, propose a palette in the strategy phase and wait for confirmation before building anything.
204	
205	**Tool options:**
206	
207	Pick the engine per animation slot. Do not default to Remotion just because the animation is web-adjacent.
208	
209	- **HyperFrames** — Browser-native HTML/CSS/GSAP video compositions: product UI motion, website-to-video or mockup-to-video captures, kinetic typography, landing-page/storyboard promos, data-driven UI states, transparent WebM overlays, and clips that need deterministic frame capture plus HyperFrames lint/validate/render checks. Best when the animation should be authored and verified like a web composition instead of a React component tree.
210	- **Remotion** — React/CSS compositions with component state, reusable React primitives, or an existing Remotion brand system. Best when the user specifically asks for React/Remotion or when React composition is the simpler authoring model.
211	- **Manim** — formal diagrams, state machines, equation derivations, graph morphs. Read `skills/manim-video/SKILL.md` and its references for depth.
212	- **PIL + PNG sequence + ffmpeg** — simple overlay cards: counters, typewriter text, single bar reveals, progressive draws. Fast to iterate, any aesthetic you want. The launch video used this.
213	
214	For HyperFrames slots, scaffold the slot inside `edit/animations/slot_<id>/` with `npx --yes hyperframes init . --example blank --non-interactive --skip-skills`, build the HTML composition there, run the HyperFrames checks that fit the slot (`lint`, `validate`, and a draft render when practical), then produce the final overlay video with `npx --yes hyperframes render . -o render.mp4` or `--format webm -o render.webm` when alpha is required. Point the EDL overlay `file` at the actual rendered path.
215	
216	For Remotion slots, keep the Remotion project isolated inside the same slot directory, scaffold with `npx create-video@latest` or install Remotion locally there, render the composition to `render.mp4` with the project-local `remotion render` command, and verify duration and dimensions with `ffprobe`.
217	
218	None is mandatory. Invent hybrids if useful (e.g., PIL background with a HyperFrames or Remotion layer on top).
219	
220	**Duration rules of thumb, context-dependent:**
221	
222	- **Sync-to-narration explanations.** A viewer needs to parse the content at 1×. Rough floor 3s, typical 5–7s for simple cards, 8–14s for complex diagrams. The launch video shipped at 5–7s per simple card.
223	- **Beat-synced accents** (music video, fast montage). 0.5–2s is fine — they're visual accents, not information. The "readable at 1×" rule becomes *"recognizable at 1×"*, not *"fully parseable."*
224	- **Hold the final frame ≥ 1s** before the cut (universal).
225	- **Over voiceover:** total duration ≥ `narration_length + 1s` (universal).
226	- **Never parallel-reveal independent elements** — the eye can't track two new things at once. One thing, pause, next thing.
227	
228	**Animation payoff timing (rule for sync-to-narration):** get the payoff word's timestamp. Start the overlay `reveal_duration` seconds earlier so the landing frame coincides with the spoken payoff word. Without this sync the animation feels disconnected.
229	
230	**Easing** (universal — never `linear`, it looks robotic):
231	
232	```python
233	def ease_out_cubic(t):    return 1 - (1 - t) ** 3
234	def ease_in_out_cubic(t):
235	    if t < 0.5: return 4 * t ** 3
236	    return 1 - (-2 * t + 2) ** 3 / 2
237	```
238	
239	`ease_out_cubic` for single reveals (slow landing). `ease_in_out_cubic` for continuous draws.
240	
241	**Typing text anchor trick:** center on the FULL string's width, not the partial-string width — otherwise text slides left during reveal.
242	
243	**Example palette** (the launch video — one aesthetic among infinite):
244	- Background `(10, 10, 10)` near-black
245	- Accent `#FF5A00` / `(255, 90, 0)` orange
246	- Labels `(110, 110, 110)` dim gray
247	- Font: Menlo Bold at `/System/Library/Fonts/Menlo.ttc` (index 1)
248	- ≤ 2 accent colors, ~40% empty space, minimal chrome
249	- Result: terminal / retro tech feel
250	
251	This is one style. If the brand is warm and serif, use that. If it's colorful and playful, use that. If the user handed you a style guide, follow it. If they didn't, propose one and confirm.
252	
253	**Fonts fail silently.** A web font that didn't load renders in a fallback face with no error — the video ships in "almost Arial". In HyperFrames/Remotion, await the font load and then assert it: `if (!document.fonts.check('700 76px "Inter"')) throw new Error(...)`. In PIL, pass an explicit font path; never rely on the default.
254	
255	**Worked example — "show the edit" hook** (a launch video for this tool). Instead of a title card, the first 3s visualize the editing itself: each transcript word pops in on its Scribe timestamp, with bars under it drawn from the real audio envelope; a filler ("ummm") grows letter by letter while it is spoken, turns orange and is cut out on screen at the same frame the audio cuts, and the next line lands immediately. It works because the picture is *driven by the same data as the sound* — one composition (Remotion) reads frame-exact word/envelope JSON produced in Python, so nothing can drift. Use the idea whenever the story is "we removed something": make the removal visible.
256	
257	**Parallel sub-agent brief** — each animation is one sub-agent spawned via the `Agent` tool. Each prompt is self-contained (sub-agents have no parent context). Include:
258	
259	1. One-sentence goal: *"Build ONE animation: [spec]. Nothing else."*
260	2. Absolute output path (`<edit>/animations/slot_<id>/render.mp4`)
261	3. Exact technical spec: resolution, fps, codec, pix_fmt, CRF, duration
262	4. Style palette as concrete values (RGB tuples, hex, or reference to a design system)
263	5. Font path with index
264	6. Frame-by-frame timeline (what happens when, with easing)
265	7. Anti-list ("no chrome, no extras, no titles unless specified")
266	8. Code pattern reference (copy helpers inline, don't import across slots)
267	9. Deliverable checklist (script, render, verify duration via ffprobe, report)
268	10. **"Do not ask questions. If anything is ambiguous, pick the most obvious interpretation and proceed."**
269	
270	One sub-agent = one file (unique filenames, parallel agents don't overwrite each other).
271	
272	## Music and sound effects (when requested)
273	
274	Sound is where generated videos sound cheap. Worked rules from launch edits:
275	
276	- **Fewer effects.** Every effect is tied to something visible (a cut, a landing, a click). ~20 stock whooshes/risers/impacts in 18s reads as generic; ~8 reads as designed.
277	- **Hit on the frame.** Most effects have an attack (silence or a build before the transient). Measure it (first sample above ~-30 dBFS of the peak) and start the file `attack` seconds *before* the visible contact frame.
278	- **Duck music under speech** (roughly -12 to -15 dB relative to its music-only level), and ramp it out before a stinger or end card instead of letting its own tail decay under your CTA.
279	- **Master once:** mix to PCM, then two-pass loudnorm (-14 LUFS, true peak ≤ -1 dBTP) on the final mix. Then measure per section (see Self-eval).
280	- **Music taste is the user's call.** Generated music defaults to "hype"; offer two contrasting beds and let the user listen. Don't claim a mix sounds good — you can only measure it.
281	
282	## Output spec
283	
284	Match the source unless the user asked for something specific. Common targets: `1920×1080@24` cinematic, `1920×1080@30` screen content, `1080×1920@30` vertical social, `3840×2160@24` 4K cinema, `1080×1080@30` square. `render.py` defaults the scale to 1080p from any source; pass `--filter` or edit the extract command for other targets. Worth asking the user which delivery format matters.
285	
286	## EDL format
287	
288	```json
289	{
290	  "version": 1,
291	  "sources": {"C0103": "/abs/path/C0103.MP4", "C0108": "/abs/path/C0108.MP4"},
292	  "ranges": [
293	    {"source": "C0103", "start": 2.42, "end": 6.85,
294	     "beat": "HOOK", "quote": "...", "reason": "Cleanest delivery, stops before slip at 38.46."},
295	    {"source": "C0108", "start": 14.30, "end": 28.90,
296	     "beat": "SOLUTION", "quote": "...", "reason": "Only take without the false start."}
297	  ],
298	  "grade": "warm_cinematic",
299	  "overlays": [
300	    {"file": "edit/animations/slot_1/render.mp4", "start_in_output": 0.0, "duration": 5.0}
301	  ],
302	  "subtitles": "edit/master.srt",
303	  "total_duration_s": 87.4
304	}
305	```
306	
307	`grade` is a preset name or raw ffmpeg filter. `overlays` are rendered animation clips. `subtitles` is optional and applied LAST.
308	
309	## Memory — `project.md`
310	
311	Append one section per session at `<edit>/project.md`:
312	
313	```markdown
314	## Session N — YYYY-MM-DD
315	
316	**Strategy:** one paragraph describing the approach
317	**Decisions:** take choices, cuts, grades, animations + why
318	**Reasoning log:** one-line rationale for non-obvious decisions
319	**Outstanding:** deferred items
320	```
321	
322	On startup, read `project.md` if it exists and summarize the last session in one sentence before asking whether to continue.
323	
324	## Anti-patterns
325	
326	Things that consistently fail regardless of style:
327	
328	- **Hierarchical pre-computed codec formats** with USABILITY / tone tags / shot layers. Over-engineering. Derive from the transcript at decision time.
329	- **Hand-tuned moment-scoring functions.** The LLM picks better than any heuristic you'll write.
330	- **Whisper SRT / phrase-level output.** Loses sub-second gap data. Always word-level verbatim.
331	- **Running Whisper locally on CPU.** Slow and it normalizes fillers. Use hosted Scribe.
332	- **Burning subtitles into base before compositing overlays.** Overlays hide them. (Hard Rule 1.)
333	- **Single-pass filtergraph when you have overlays.** Double re-encodes. Use per-segment extract → concat.
334	- **Linear animation easing.** Looks robotic. Always cubic.
335	- **Unverified web fonts.** A failed load silently falls back to a system face. Assert the font loaded before rendering.
336	- **Stock SFX on every transition.** Tie each effect to a visible event; cap the count.
337	- **Hard audio cuts at segment boundaries.** Audible pops. (Hard Rule 3.)
338	- **Typing text centered on the partial string.** Text slides left as it grows.
339	- **Sequential sub-agents for multiple animations.** Always parallel.
340	- **Editing before confirming the strategy.** Never.
341	- **Re-transcribing cached sources.** Immutable outputs of immutable inputs.
342	- **Assuming what kind of video it is.** Look first, ask second, edit last.
343

---
name: video-use
description: Edit any video by conversation. Transcribe, cut, color grade, generate overlay animations, burn subtitles — for talking heads, montages, tutorials, travel, interviews. No presets, no menus. Ask questions, confirm the plan, execute, iterate, persist. Production-correctness rules are hard; everything else is artistic freedom.
---

# Video Use

## Principle

1. **LLM reasons from raw transcript + on-demand visuals.** The only derived artifact that earns its keep is a packed phrase-level transcript (`takes_packed.md`). Everything else — filler tagging, retake detection, shot classification, emphasis scoring — you derive at decision time.
2. **Audio is primary, visuals follow.** Cut candidates come from speech boundaries and silence gaps. Drill into visuals only at decision points.
3. **Ask → confirm → execute → iterate → persist.** Never touch the cut until the user has confirmed the strategy in plain English.
4. **Generalize.** Do not assume what kind of video this is. Look at the material, ask the user, then edit.
5. **Artistic freedom is the default.** Every specific value, preset, font, color, duration, pitch structure, and technique in this document is a *worked example* from one proven video — not a mandate. Read them to understand what's possible and why each worked. Then make your own taste calls based on what the material actually is and what the user actually wants. **The only things you MUST do are in the Hard Rules section below.** Everything else is yours.
6. **Invent freely.** If the material calls for a technique not described here — split-screen, picture-in-picture, lower-third identity cards, reaction cuts, speed ramps, freeze frames, crossfades, match cuts, L-cuts, J-cuts, speed ramps over breath, whatever — build it. The helpers are ffmpeg and PIL. They can do anything the format supports. Do not wait for permission.
7. **Verify your own output before showing it to the user.** If you wouldn't ship it, don't present it.

## Hard Rules (production correctness — non-negotiable)

These are the things where deviation produces silent failures or broken output. They are not taste, they are correctness. Memorize them.

1. **Subtitles are applied LAST in the filter chain**, after every overlay. Otherwise overlays hide captions. Silent failure.
2. **Per-segment extract → lossless `-c copy` concat**, not single-pass filtergraph. Otherwise you double-encode every segment when overlays are added.
3. **30ms audio fades at every segment boundary** (`afade=t=in:st=0:d=0.03,afade=t=out:st={dur-0.03}:d=0.03`). Otherwise audible pops at every cut.
4. **Overlays use `setpts=PTS-STARTPTS+T/TB`** to shift the overlay's frame 0 to its window start. Otherwise you see the middle of the animation during the overlay window.
5. **Master SRT uses output-timeline offsets**: `output_time = word.start - segment_start + segment_offset`. Otherwise captions misalign after segment concat.
6. **Never cut inside a word.** Snap every cut edge to a word boundary from the Scribe transcript.
7. **Pad every cut edge.** Working window: 30–200ms. Scribe timestamps drift 50–100ms — padding absorbs the drift. Tighter for fast-paced, looser for cinematic.
8. **Word-level verbatim ASR only.** Never SRT/phrase mode (loses sub-second gap data). Never normalized fillers (loses editorial signal).
9. **Cache transcripts per source.** Never re-transcribe unless the source file itself changed.
10. **Parallel sub-agents for multiple animations.** Never sequential. Spawn N at once via the `Agent` tool; total wall time ≈ slowest one.
11. **Strategy confirmation before execution.** Never touch the cut until the user has approved the plain-English plan.
12. **All session outputs in `<videos_dir>/edit/`.** Never write inside the `video-use/` project directory.

Everything else in this document is a worked example. Deviate whenever the material calls for it.

## Directory layout

The skill lives in `video-use/`. User footage lives wherever they put it. All session outputs go into `<videos_dir>/edit/`.

```
<videos_dir>/
├── <source files, untouched>
└── edit/
    ├── project.md               ← memory; appended every session
    ├── takes_packed.md          ← phrase-level transcripts, the LLM's primary reading view
    ├── edl.json                 ← cut decisions
    ├── transcripts/<name>.json  ← cached raw Scribe JSON
    ├── animations/slot_<id>/    ← per-animation source + render + reasoning
    ├── clips_graded/            ← per-segment extracts with grade + fades
    ├── master.srt               ← output-timeline subtitles
    ├── downloads/               ← yt-dlp outputs
    ├── verify/                  ← debug frames / timeline PNGs
    ├── preview.mp4
    └── final.mp4
```

## Setup

First-time install lives in `install.md` (clone, deps, ffmpeg, skill registration, API key). Don't re-run it every session; on cold start just verify:

- `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY` resolves — either in the environment or in `.env` at the video-use repo root. If missing, ask the user to paste one and write it to `.env` (never to the user's `<videos_dir>`).
- `ffmpeg` + `ffprobe` on PATH.
- Python deps installed (`uv sync` or `pip install -e .` inside the repo).
- Node.js + npm available if the session needs HyperFrames or Remotion slots. HyperFrames currently requires Node.js 22+.
- `yt-dlp`, HyperFrames, Remotion, Manim installed only on first use.
- First-use animation setup happens inside the slot directory, never at the video-use repo root. HyperFrames can be invoked with `npx --yes hyperframes ...`; Remotion can be scaffolded with `npx create-video@latest` or installed as a project-local dependency before using its `remotion render` command.
- This skill vendors `skills/manim-video/`. Read its SKILL.md when building a Manim slot.

Helpers (`helpers/transcribe.py`, `helpers/render.py`, etc.) live alongside this SKILL.md. Resolve their paths relative to the directory containing this file — the skill is typically symlinked at `~/.claude/skills/video-use/` or `~/.codex/skills/video-use/`.

## Helpers

- **`transcribe.py <video>`** — single-file Scribe call. `--num-speakers N` optional. Cached.
- **`transcribe_batch.py <videos_dir>`** — 4-worker parallel transcription. Use for multi-take.
- **`pack_transcripts.py --edit-dir <dir>`** — `transcripts/*.json` → `takes_packed.md` (phrase-level, break on silence ≥ 0.5s).
- **`timeline_view.py <video> <start> <end>`** — filmstrip + waveform PNG. On-demand visual drill-down. **Not a scan tool** — use it at decision points, not constantly.
- **`render.py <edl.json> -o <out>`** — per-segment extract → concat → overlays (PTS-shifted) → subtitles LAST. `--preview` for 720p fast. `--build-subtitles` to generate master.srt inline.
- **`grade.py <in> -o <out>`** — ffmpeg filter chain grade. Presets + `--filter '<raw>'` for custom.

For animations, create `<edit>/animations/slot_<id>/` with `Bash` and spawn a sub-agent via the `Agent` tool.

## The process

1. **Inventory.** `ffprobe` every source. `transcribe_batch.py` on the directory. `pack_transcripts.py` to produce `takes_packed.md`. Sample one or two `timeline_view`s for a visual first impression.
2. **Pre-scan for problems.** One pass over `takes_packed.md` to note verbal slips, obvious mis-speaks, or phrasings to avoid. Plain list, feed into the editor brief.
3. **Converse.** Describe what you see in plain English. Ask questions *shaped by the material*. Collect: content type, target length/aspect, aesthetic/brand direction, pacing feel, must-preserve moments, must-cut moments, animation and grade preferences, subtitle needs. Do not use a fixed checklist — the right questions are different every time.
4. **Propose strategy.** 4–8 sentences: shape, take choices, cut direction, animation plan, grade direction, subtitle style, length estimate. **Wait for confirmation.**
5. **Execute.** Produce `edl.json` via the editor sub-agent brief. Drill into `timeline_view` at ambiguous moments. Build animations in parallel sub-agents. Apply grade per-segment. Compose via `render.py`.
6. **Preview.** `render.py --preview`.
7. **Self-eval (before showing the user).** Run `timeline_view` on the **rendered output** (not the sources) at every cut boundary (±1.5s window). Check each image for:
   - Visual discontinuity / flash / jump at the cut
   - Waveform spike at the boundary (audio pop that slipped past the 30ms fade)
   - Subtitle hidden behind an overlay (Rule 1 violation)
   - Overlay misaligned or showing wrong frames (Rule 4 violation)

   Also sample: first 2s, last 2s, and 2–3 mid-points — check grade consistency, subtitle readability, overall coherence. Run `ffprobe` on the output to verify duration matches the EDL expectation.

   Measure the audio, don't assume it: `ffmpeg -i out.mp4 -af ebur128=peak=true -f null -` for integrated loudness and true peak, plus RMS per section (dialogue, music-only, end card). An end card 15 dB under the dialogue, or effects louder than speech, is a bug. You cannot listen: say so, and report the numbers.

   For anything the user will publish (launch, promo, ad), also spawn one **critic sub-agent** with the rendered file, the EDL, and any reference videos the user gave. Brief it to roast, not to praise: a verdict, ranked problems with timecodes and evidence (frames, levels), and the 5 fixes to do first. Fresh eyes catch what the author stopped seeing — cut-off payoff lines, 0.5s memes, unreadable 28px text at phone size.

   If anything fails: fix → re-render → re-eval. **Cap at 3 self-eval passes** — if issues remain after 3, flag them to the user rather than looping forever. Only present the preview once the self-eval passes.
8. **Iterate + persist.** Natural-language feedback, re-plan, re-render. Never re-transcribe. Final render on confirmation. Append to `project.md`.

## Cut craft (techniques)

- **Audio-first.** Candidate cuts from word boundaries and silence gaps.
- **Preserve peaks.** Laughs, punchlines, emphasis beats. Extend past punchlines to include reactions — the laugh IS the beat.
- **Speaker handoffs** benefit from air between utterances. Common values: 400–600ms. Less for fast-paced, more for cinematic. Taste call.
- **Audio events as signals.** `(laughs)`, `(sighs)`, `(applause)` mark beats. Extend past them.
- **Silence gaps are cut candidates.** Silences ≥400ms are usually the cleanest. 150–400ms phrase boundaries are usable with a visual check. <150ms is unsafe (mid-phrase).
- **Example cut padding** (the launch video shipped with this): 50ms before the first kept word, 80ms after the last. Tighter for montage energy, looser for documentary. Stay in the 30–200ms working window (Hard Rule 7).
- **Never reason audio and video independently.** Every cut must work on both tracks.

## The packed transcript (primary reading view)

`pack_transcripts.py` reads all `transcripts/*.json` and produces one markdown file where each take is a list of phrase-level lines, each prefixed with its `[start-end]` time range. Phrases break on any silence ≥ 0.5s OR speaker change. This is the artifact the editor sub-agent reads to pick cuts — it gives word-boundary precision from text alone at 1/10 the tokens of raw JSON.

Example line:
```
## C0103  (duration: 43.0s, 8 phrases)
  [002.52-005.36] S0 Ninety percent of what a web agent does is completely wasted.
  [006.08-006.74] S0 We fixed this.
```

## Editor sub-agent brief (for multi-take selection)

When the task is "pick the best take of each beat across many clips," spawn a dedicated sub-agent with a brief shaped like this. The structure is load-bearing; the pitch-shape example is not.

```
You are editing a <type> video. Pick the best take of each beat and 
assemble them chronologically by beat, not by source clip order.

INPUTS:
  - takes_packed.md (time-annotated phrase-level transcripts of all takes)
  - Product/narrative context: <2 sentences from the user>
  - Speaker(s): <name, role, delivery style note>
  - Expected structure: <pick an archetype or invent one>
  - Verbal slips to avoid: <list from the pre-scan pass>
  - Target runtime: <seconds>

Common structural archetypes (pick, adapt, or invent):
  - Tech launch / demo:   HOOK → PROBLEM → SOLUTION → BENEFIT → EXAMPLE → CTA
  - Tutorial:             INTRO → SETUP → STEPS → GOTCHAS → RECAP
  - Interview:            (QUESTION → ANSWER → FOLLOWUP) repeat
  - Travel / event:       ARRIVAL → HIGHLIGHTS → QUIET MOMENTS → DEPARTURE
  - Documentary:          THESIS → EVIDENCE → COUNTERPOINT → CONCLUSION
  - Music / performance:  INTRO → VERSE → CHORUS → BRIDGE → OUTRO
  - Or invent your own.

RULES:
  - Start/end times must fall on word boundaries from the transcript.
  - Pad cut boundaries (working window 30–200ms).
  - Prefer silences ≥ 400ms as cut targets.
  - Unavoidable slips are kept if no better take exists. Note them in "reason".
  - If over budget, revise: drop a beat or trim tails. Report total and self-correct.

OUTPUT (JSON array, no prose):
  [{"source": "C0103", "start": 2.42, "end": 6.85, "beat": "HOOK",
    "quote": "...", "reason": "..."}, ...]

```

## Color grade (when requested)

Your job is to **reason about the image**, not apply a preset. Look at a frame (via `timeline_view`), decide what's wrong, adjust one thing, look again.

Mental model is ASC CDL. Per channel: `out = (in * slope + offset) ** power`, then global saturation. `slope` → highlights, `offset` → shadows, `power` → midtones.

**Example filter chains** (`grade.py` has `--list-presets`; use them as starting points or mix your own):

- **`warm_cinematic`** — retro/technical, subtle teal/orange split, desaturated. Shipped in a real launch video. Safe for talking heads.
- **`neutral_punch`** — minimal corrective: contrast bump + gentle S-curve. No hue shifts.
- **`none`** — straight copy. Default when the user hasn't asked.

For anything else — portraiture, nature, product, music video, documentary — invent your own chain. `grade.py --filter '<raw ffmpeg>'` accepts any filter string.

Hard rules: apply **per-segment during extraction** (not post-concat, which re-encodes twice). Never go aggressive without testing skin tones.

## Subtitles (when requested)

Subtitles have three dimensions worth reasoning about: **chunking** (1/2/3/sentence per line), **case** (UPPER/Title/Natural), and **placement** (margin from bottom). The right combo depends on content.

**Worked styles** — pick, adapt, or invent:

**`bold-overlay`** — short-form tech launch, fast-paced social. ~2-word chunks, UPPERCASE, break on punctuation and pauses ≥ 0.3s, grow to 3 words rather than flash a cue < 0.35s (`chunk_words` in `render.py`), Helvetica 18 Bold, white-on-outline, `MarginV=35`. `render.py` ships with this as `SUB_FORCE_STYLE`.

```
FontName=Helvetica,FontSize=18,Bold=1,
PrimaryColour=&H00FFFFFF,OutlineColour=&H00000000,BackColour=&H00000000,
BorderStyle=1,Outline=2,Shadow=0,
Alignment=2,MarginV=35
```

**`natural-sentence`** (if you invent this mode) — narrative, documentary, education. 4–7 word chunks, sentence case, break on natural pauses, `MarginV=60–80`, larger font for readability, slightly wider max-width. No shipped force_style — design one if you need it.

Invent a third style if neither fits. Hard rules: subtitles LAST (Rule 1), output-timeline offsets (Rule 5).

## Animations (when requested)

Animations match the content and the brand. **Get the palette, font, and visual language from the conversation** — never assume a default. If the user hasn't told you, propose a palette in the strategy phase and wait for confirmation before building anything.

**Tool options:**

Pick the engine per animation slot. Do not default to Remotion just because the animation is web-adjacent.

- **HyperFrames** — Browser-native HTML/CSS/GSAP video compositions: product UI motion, website-to-video or mockup-to-video captures, kinetic typography, landing-page/storyboard promos, data-driven UI states, transparent WebM overlays, and clips that need deterministic frame capture plus HyperFrames lint/validate/render checks. Best when the animation should be authored and verified like a web composition instead of a React component tree.
- **Remotion** — React/CSS compositions with component state, reusable React primitives, or an existing Remotion brand system. Best when the user specifically asks for React/Remotion or when React composition is the simpler authoring model.
- **Manim** — formal diagrams, state machines, equation derivations, graph morphs. Read `skills/manim-video/SKILL.md` and its references for depth.
- **PIL + PNG sequence + ffmpeg** — simple overlay cards: counters, typewriter text, single bar reveals, progressive draws. Fast to iterate, any aesthetic you want. The launch video used this.

For HyperFrames slots, scaffold the slot inside `edit/animations/slot_<id>/` with `npx --yes hyperframes init . --example blank --non-interactive --skip-skills`, build the HTML composition there, run the HyperFrames checks that fit the slot (`lint`, `validate`, and a draft render when practical), then produce the final overlay video with `npx --yes hyperframes render . -o render.mp4` or `--format webm -o render.webm` when alpha is required. Point the EDL overlay `file` at the actual rendered path.

For Remotion slots, keep the Remotion project isolated inside the same slot directory, scaffold with `npx create-video@latest` or install Remotion locally there, render the composition to `render.mp4` with the project-local `remotion render` command, and verify duration and dimensions with `ffprobe`.

None is mandatory. Invent hybrids if useful (e.g., PIL background with a HyperFrames or Remotion layer on top).

**Duration rules of thumb, context-dependent:**

- **Sync-to-narration explanations.** A viewer needs to parse the content at 1×. Rough floor 3s, typical 5–7s for simple cards, 8–14s for complex diagrams. The launch video shipped at 5–7s per simple card.
- **Beat-synced accents** (music video, fast montage). 0.5–2s is fine — they're visual accents, not information. The "readable at 1×" rule becomes *"recognizable at 1×"*, not *"fully parseable."*
- **Hold the final frame ≥ 1s** before the cut (universal).
- **Over voiceover:** total duration ≥ `narration_length + 1s` (universal).
- **Never parallel-reveal independent elements** — the eye can't track two new things at once. One thing, pause, next thing.

**Animation payoff timing (rule for sync-to-narration):** get the payoff word's timestamp. Start the overlay `reveal_duration` seconds earlier so the landing frame coincides with the spoken payoff word. Without this sync the animation feels disconnected.

**Easing** (universal — never `linear`, it looks robotic):

```python
def ease_out_cubic(t):    return 1 - (1 - t) ** 3
def ease_in_out_cubic(t):
    if t < 0.5: return 4 * t ** 3
    return 1 - (-2 * t + 2) ** 3 / 2
```

`ease_out_cubic` for single reveals (slow landing). `ease_in_out_cubic` for continuous draws.

**Typing text anchor trick:** center on the FULL string's width, not the partial-string width — otherwise text slides left during reveal.

**Example palette** (the launch video — one aesthetic among infinite):
- Background `(10, 10, 10)` near-black
- Accent `#FF5A00` / `(255, 90, 0)` orange
- Labels `(110, 110, 110)` dim gray
- Font: Menlo Bold at `/System/Library/Fonts/Menlo.ttc` (index 1)
- ≤ 2 accent colors, ~40% empty space, minimal chrome
- Result: terminal / retro tech feel

This is one style. If the brand is warm and serif, use that. If it's colorful and playful, use that. If the user handed you a style guide, follow it. If they didn't, propose one and confirm.

**Fonts fail silently.** A web font that didn't load renders in a fallback face with no error — the video ships in "almost Arial". In HyperFrames/Remotion, await the font load and then assert it: `if (!document.fonts.check('700 76px "Inter"')) throw new Error(...)`. In PIL, pass an explicit font path; never rely on the default.

**Worked example — "show the edit" hook** (a launch video for this tool). Instead of a title card, the first 3s visualize the editing itself: each transcript word pops in on its Scribe timestamp, with bars under it drawn from the real audio envelope; a filler ("ummm") grows letter by letter while it is spoken, turns orange and is cut out on screen at the same frame the audio cuts, and the next line lands immediately. It works because the picture is *driven by the same data as the sound* — one composition (Remotion) reads frame-exact word/envelope JSON produced in Python, so nothing can drift. Use the idea whenever the story is "we removed something": make the removal visible.

**Parallel sub-agent brief** — each animation is one sub-agent spawned via the `Agent` tool. Each prompt is self-contained (sub-agents have no parent context). Include:

1. One-sentence goal: *"Build ONE animation: [spec]. Nothing else."*
2. Absolute output path (`<edit>/animations/slot_<id>/render.mp4`)
3. Exact technical spec: resolution, fps, codec, pix_fmt, CRF, duration
4. Style palette as concrete values (RGB tuples, hex, or reference to a design system)
5. Font path with index
6. Frame-by-frame timeline (what happens when, with easing)
7. Anti-list ("no chrome, no extras, no titles unless specified")
8. Code pattern reference (copy helpers inline, don't import across slots)
9. Deliverable checklist (script, render, verify duration via ffprobe, report)
10. **"Do not ask questions. If anything is ambiguous, pick the most obvious interpretation and proceed."**

One sub-agent = one file (unique filenames, parallel agents don't overwrite each other).

## Music and sound effects (when requested)

Sound is where generated videos sound cheap. Worked rules from launch edits:

- **Fewer effects.** Every effect is tied to something visible (a cut, a landing, a click). ~20 stock whooshes/risers/impacts in 18s reads as generic; ~8 reads as designed.
- **Hit on the frame.** Most effects have an attack (silence or a build before the transient). Measure it (first sample above ~-30 dBFS of the peak) and start the file `attack` seconds *before* the visible contact frame.
- **Duck music under speech** (roughly -12 to -15 dB relative to its music-only level), and ramp it out before a stinger or end card instead of letting its own tail decay under your CTA.
- **Master once:** mix to PCM, then two-pass loudnorm (-14 LUFS, true peak ≤ -1 dBTP) on the final mix. Then measure per section (see Self-eval).
- **Music taste is the user's call.** Generated music defaults to "hype"; offer two contrasting beds and let the user listen. Don't claim a mix sounds good — you can only measure it.

## Output spec

Match the source unless the user asked for something specific. Common targets: `1920×1080@24` cinematic, `1920×1080@30` screen content, `1080×1920@30` vertical social, `3840×2160@24` 4K cinema, `1080×1080@30` square. `render.py` defaults the scale to 1080p from any source; pass `--filter` or edit the extract command for other targets. Worth asking the user which delivery format matters.

## EDL format

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "sources": {"C0103": "/abs/path/C0103.MP4", "C0108": "/abs/path/C0108.MP4"},
  "ranges": [
    {"source": "C0103", "start": 2.42, "end": 6.85,
     "beat": "HOOK", "quote": "...", "reason": "Cleanest delivery, stops before slip at 38.46."},
    {"source": "C0108", "start": 14.30, "end": 28.90,
     "beat": "SOLUTION", "quote": "...", "reason": "Only take without the false start."}
  ],
  "grade": "warm_cinematic",
  "overlays": [
    {"file": "edit/animations/slot_1/render.mp4", "start_in_output": 0.0, "duration": 5.0}
  ],
  "subtitles": "edit/master.srt",
  "total_duration_s": 87.4
}
```

`grade` is a preset name or raw ffmpeg filter. `overlays` are rendered animation clips. `subtitles` is optional and applied LAST.

## Memory — `project.md`

Append one section per session at `<edit>/project.md`:

```markdown
## Session N — YYYY-MM-DD

**Strategy:** one paragraph describing the approach
**Decisions:** take choices, cuts, grades, animations + why
**Reasoning log:** one-line rationale for non-obvious decisions
**Outstanding:** deferred items
```

On startup, read `project.md` if it exists and summarize the last session in one sentence before asking whether to continue.

## Anti-patterns

Things that consistently fail regardless of style:

- **Hierarchical pre-computed codec formats** with USABILITY / tone tags / shot layers. Over-engineering. Derive from the transcript at decision time.
- **Hand-tuned moment-scoring functions.** The LLM picks better than any heuristic you'll write.
- **Whisper SRT / phrase-level output.** Loses sub-second gap data. Always word-level verbatim.
- **Running Whisper locally on CPU.** Slow and it normalizes fillers. Use hosted Scribe.
- **Burning subtitles into base before compositing overlays.** Overlays hide them. (Hard Rule 1.)
- **Single-pass filtergraph when you have overlays.** Double re-encodes. Use per-segment extract → concat.
- **Linear animation easing.** Looks robotic. Always cubic.
- **Unverified web fonts.** A failed load silently falls back to a system face. Assert the font loaded before rendering.
- **Stock SFX on every transition.** Tie each effect to a visible event; cap the count.
- **Hard audio cuts at segment boundaries.** Audible pops. (Hard Rule 3.)
- **Typing text centered on the partial string.** Text slides left as it grows.
- **Sequential sub-agents for multiple animations.** Always parallel.
- **Editing before confirming the strategy.** Never.
- **Re-transcribing cached sources.** Immutable outputs of immutable inputs.
- **Assuming what kind of video it is.** Look first, ask second, edit last.

content.text:
The edit is finished and rendered to `edit/final.mp4`.

**Deliverable:** `edit/final.mp4` is 11.30 s, 1920×1080, 16:9, 30 fps, H.264/AAC, at −14.1 LUFS with a −1.7 dBTP true peak. Captions are burned in, and `edit/final.srt` is next to it as an upload sidecar.

**The edit:**
- **Cut:** I removed Dana's false start ("Today we're launching... Um, sorry, let me start that again."). The video runs "Hi, I'm Dana from ACME Studio." straight into the clean second take, ending on "Try it this week". The cut falls in a pause and the waveform shows no pop.
- **Graphics:** there are three:
  - a "Dana / ACME STUDIO" name card while she introduces herself;
  - a "Studio Engine" title landing on "Studio";
  - a yellow "Try it this week" button landing on "Try".
  
  The last picture frame is then frozen for 1.2 s with the title and button still on screen.
- **Captions:** up to 4 words a line, with the spoken word highlighted in yellow and a heavy black outline so they stay readable over the colour bars.
- **Review:** a separate critic pass flagged four problems: no end hold, both graphics arriving early, awkward caption line breaks, and a rushed breath at the cut. I fixed all four, re-rendered, and checked the frames again.

**Assumptions I made:**
- No brief, brand files or music came with the job. The look is my default: Inter font, white text, yellow #FFD60A, dark panels.
- The size matches the source (16:9). There's no vertical version.
- The colour is left as shot.
- There's no music, since none was supplied.
- The picture is a colour-bar test pattern, which I treated as the real footage.

**Not done:** the Homebrew ffmpeg on this Mac has no libass, so video-use's own caption burn-in doesn't work. I built the captions in HyperFrames instead, so nothing is missing from the final.

Everything is in `edit/`: the cut list (`edl.json`), the plan and decisions (`project.md`), the transcript and the graphics sources.
